first.rationale: Onboarding deterioration is a current upstream constraint on activation, and two inherited findings indicate that reducing friction improved completion, time-to-value, and durable SMB activation. A controlled experiment is preferable to immediately discounting because the primary objective is sustainable qualified revenue; downstream conversion, retention, and revenue quality should remain explicit guardrails.

final.rationale: Run a controlled onboarding-simplification experiment, prioritizing SMB users. The verified evidence directly addresses both current declines: shorter onboarding raised completion 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and improved 30-day retention 3%; SMB signup simplification raised activation 9% and qualified revenue 4%. Because the latter also reduced 30-day retention 1% and was not replicated beyond SMB, monitor retention and qualified revenue as guardrails and avoid extrapolating to other segments.
